newsitem.title: USA: Williams Co to reorganize its five-pipeline system.
newsitem.headline: Williams Co to reorganize its five-pipeline system.

text.p: The Williams Cos said Tuesday it plans to reorganize its five independent natural gas pipeline companies into one national entity to better compete in the marketplace.

Williams chief executive Brian E O'Neill said in a statement the changes will be effective July 1 and transform the company's five interstate systems "into a more seamless national transportation company."

Williams' five gas systems and their headquarters are: Kern River and Northwest Pipeline in Salt Lake City; Williams Natural Gas, in Tulsa, Oklahoma; Transco in Houston; and Texas Gas in Owensboro, Kentucky.
The pipelines, each currently independently structured, will create a new shared services organization, the statement said.

David Young, currently senior vice president and chief operating officer of Williams Learning Network, will become senior vice president and general manager of shared services, reporting to O'Neill, the statement said.

Reporting to Young will be Nick Bacile, currently vice president of finance and controller at Transco. Bacile will be the vice president and chief financial officer with responsibility for the five pipeline systems' accounting and financial functions.
